## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.9`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noUselessDefaultAssignment`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`types`](/linter/domains#types)
- Sources: 
  - Inspired from [`@typescript-eslint/no-useless-default-assignment`](https://typescript-eslint.io/rules/no-useless-default-assignment)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noUselessDefaultAssignment": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow default values that can never be used.

A default value only applies when the value it replaces is `undefined`.
If the type says the value can't be `undefined`, the default is dead code.

This rule checks destructured object properties, destructured tuple
elements, and parameters of callbacks passed directly to a call.

## Examples

### Invalid

```ts title='invalid-parameter-property.ts'
function greet({ name = "friend" }: { name: string }) {
    return `Hello, ${name}`;
}
```

### Valid

```ts
function greet({ name = "friend" }: { name?: string }) {
    return `Hello, ${name}`;
}

const { label = "none" } = { label: undefined };

declare const names: string[];
const [first = "nobody"] = names;

declare function onMessage(listener: (message?: string) => void): void;
onMessage((message = "") => console.log(message));
```

## See Also

- If you want to remove default values that are `undefined`, see [`noUselessUndefined`](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-useless-undefined/).
